description.text: Carlo Lombardi, born in 1559 in Arezzo, was an Italian architect who flourished during the late Renaissance and early Baroque periods, primarily working in Rome.

His architectural portfolio includes the Palazzo Aldobrandini in the Quirinal district, the facade of Santa Prisca, and the villa Giustinianini outside Porta del Popolo, as well as a marble portico and facade for the church of Santa Francesca Romana in the Roman Forum, commissioned by Pope Paul V and the Olivetan monks.

curiosities.text: Lombardi authored a book on the flooding of the Tiber River, reflecting his interest in hydraulic engineering.
The marble portico and facade he designed for Santa Francesca Romana were specifically commissioned during the reign of Pope Paul V.
His work on the facade of Santa Prisca demonstrates his contribution to the architectural embellishment of Rome’s churches.
